A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REFUEL study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-turn dialogue experiments on UltraInteract and Anthropic HH, with winrates, reward scores, convergence plots, and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated RLOO variants in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same on-policy roll-ins, shared-prefix resets, paired rollouts, and regression of policy log-ratios to trajectory-reward differences. The new Gauss–Newton discussion analyzes the existing objective; it does not introduce an implemented update procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate UltraInteract with a Llama-3.1-70B-it user simulator and evaluate Anthropic HH and UltraInteract with pre-sampled questions. The appendix examples and represented tasks are retained; RLOO adds comparisons within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a policy-gradient comparator family: RLOO-LT-OFFLINE, RLOO-LT-MIXED, RLOO-LT-ONLINE, and RLOO-MT-MIXED in Table 1, plus the latter three variants on both datasets in Table 2. Existing DPO, REBEL, and Llama comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The reported splits, filtering, dialogue lengths, model configurations, evaluation metrics, and 500-sample winrate evaluations remain unchanged. RLOO uses the existing last-turn and multi-turn data-collection regimes. Regrouping the DPO and REBEL hyperparameter rows does not change their settings.

E4.justification: The added RLOO variants extend the existing analysis of roll-in source and last-turn versus multi-turn optimization to another optimizer. The weighted-winrate analysis, convergence plots, qualitative comparisons, and example generations in the appendices remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's variance-reduction discussion is theoretical analysis, not a change in empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add substantial RLOO results across both settings. Table 1 adds average winrates of 46.40, 44.32, 48.00, and 50.20; Table 2 adds winrates, reward scores, and KL values for three variants per dataset. Existing results remain unchanged, including REFUEL's 56.64 average in Table 1 and 82.8/79.6 winrates in Table 2.

T1.justification: v2 retains Theorem 1, the APC condition, Propositions 1–2, and their proofs, while extending the comparison to advantage-based NPG through Equations 8–9. New Section 3.2.2 derives a linearized Gauss–Newton connection, and Claim 1 establishes an unbiased empirical Fisher estimator and the minimum-norm update, with a new proof in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: critic-free multi-turn optimization, guarantees against covered policies under weaker conditions than NPG, and improved longer-dialogue performance. The new analysis and RLOO results support rather than redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations based on unrestricted state-dependent offsets and interprets the linearized update as an RLOO-like gradient with Fisher preconditioning and variance reduction. Existing empirical interpretations remain largely unchanged. The simulator and five-turn limitations are retained verbatim in Appendix J.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds Setting One hyperparameters for RLOO: batch size 128, learning rate 3e-7, weight decay 1e-6, cosine decay, and warmup ratio 0.1. Existing implementation details, hardware, training times, prompts, and code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged, but v2 explicitly emphasizes the shared REBEL update formulation and develops REFUEL's relationship to advantage-based NPG and RLOO. The existing discussion of policy optimization and resetting is moved to Appendix I rather than removed.

P1.justification: v2 introduces theoretical subsections, makes localized explanatory and grammatical edits, removes a redundant display of the existing loss, and relocates related-work material and limitations to appendices. It also adds acknowledgements and a conference header. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain RLOO blocks, and the hyperparameter table groups methods sharing settings. Figure 1 is resized and rearranged, and implementation and simulator details share a page. Figure 2 and the remaining appendix displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The RLOO comparisons broaden the empirical assessment beyond DPO and REBEL, while the new NPG/Gauss–Newton analysis and Appendix C proof strengthen understanding of the existing method. Integration is incomplete: Section 4.2 retains a blanket online-roll-in claim despite RLOO-MT-MIXED averaging 50.20 versus 48.00 for RLOO-LT-ONLINE. These additions provide a limited net improvement to an otherwise largely retained scientific case.
